note: What both servers did when the Supabase examples project was served
by each of them and every function in it was asked the same question.
A function ran when its own code or its own library produced the
outcome: a refusal from the gateway in front of it, a config error out
of the library it imports, a throw from the handler. A function did not
run when the module never finished loading or when it reached for a
runtime api that is not there. Which of the two happened is read off
the server log rather than off the status, because both of them are a
500 from the outside.
The bodies are the first 300 bytes, with tabs and newlines flattened,
which is how the probe wrote them down.
This is a recording rather than a suite: nothing in CI compares against
it. It is the denominator for a claim about the corpus, and the reason
every name that is not shared is not shared.
wasm-modules is asked of one server and not the other, which is not a
gap in the probe. Its handler imports a file a wasm build writes and
the build has not been run, so the file is not there. zou serves the
other thirty nine and answers 500 for that one. The CLI refuses to
start the stack at all while the function is in the directory, so the
way to ask upstream anything else about this project is to take the
function out of it, which is what the reference copy has done.
One of zou's answers moved again, and it is the same function each
time. custom-jwt-validation asked for AbortSignal.timeout, then for
structuredClone, and now gets as far as upstream does: both servers
refuse the same jwks for the same reason. The bodies still differ by
the name of the error class, which is a letter here because esm.sh
serves jose minified and the class names its errors after itself.
Nothing else in the corpus moved and the byte identical count is
still twenty of forty.
zou was asked again on 2026-08-19, with the reference column left as
it was: nothing about the other server changed and it was not started
for this. Two names moved and both are the same fix. oak-server ran,
and answers upstream's own 405 with upstream's own empty body, which
makes it the twenty first name the two servers answer byte for byte.
connect-supabase loads, dispatches through oak and reaches its session
store, which asks crypto.subtle for an AES-CBC key and is told there
is only HMAC here, so it is still a name upstream serves and this does
not, for a smaller reason than before.
zou was asked again on 2026-08-19 after crypto.subtle learned AES,
with the reference column left as it was. One name moved.
connect-supabase reaches its session store, which asks for an AES-CBC
key and now gets one, and the answer is upstream's own 405 with
upstream's own empty body. Seven names are left that upstream serves
and this does not, and five of the seven are the registry rather than
the runtime.
zou was asked again on 2026-08-19 after it learned where a package
file is, with the reference column left as it was. One name moved.
image-manipulation reads the wasm blob that sits beside the module the
registry served, which upstream reaches through a directory on disk
and this reaches through a url, and then it initialises fourteen
megabytes of ImageMagick and answers the same 401 upstream answers,
byte for byte. Six names are left that upstream serves and this does
not, and five of the six are the registry rather than the runtime.
zou was asked again on 2026-08-19 after it learned to open a socket,
with the reference column left as it was. One name moved.
postgres-on-the-edge imports a postgres driver, which connects to the
engine on the port the project's own config names, authenticates,
runs a select and is told by postgres that the table is not there.
That is the same sentence upstream is told, byte for byte, and it is
the twenty fourth name the two servers answer identically. Five names
are left that upstream serves and this does not, and all five of them
are the registry rather than the runtime.
One row was read twice before it was written down. oak-server came
back 546 on the first pass of that run, which is the host saying a
function spent more than the two seconds of cpu it is allowed, and it
was the first load of a module graph that large on a cold cache. Warm
it answers the 405 that is recorded here, three times out of three.
